description: Experience the fiery flavors and smoky aroma of authentic Tandoori Chicken, expertly cooked on a charcoal grill. Each succulent piece of chicken is marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic Indian spices, ensuring a tender, juicy bite every time. This classic Indian dish is perfect for a vibrant dinner, bringing the taste of the tandoor to your backyard.

ingredients.notes: cut into 8-10 pieces, make deep gashes

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the chicken pieces and pat them dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep gashes on each piece, especially on thicker parts, to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply. This ensures maximum flavor.

instructions.title: First Marinade Application
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with half of the ginger-garlic paste, half of the Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice. Rub this mixture evenly over all the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: While the chicken rests, prepare the second marinade. In a separate bowl, whisk together the drained yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, remaining Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, remaining salt, black pepper, remaining lemon juice, mustard oil, and optional red food coloring. Mix until well combined and smooth.

instructions.title: Second Marinade and Chilling
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces from the first marinade into the bowl with the second marinade. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer it marinates, the better the taste.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create a medium-high heat zone. Once the coals are ash-gray and glowing red, and the grill grates are hot, lightly oil the grates to prevent sticking. This initial heat is crucial for a good sear.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot, oiled grill grates. Grill for 6-8 minutes per side, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking and charring. Baste the chicken with any remaining marinade or a little extra oil during the last few minutes of cooking to keep it moist and flavorful. The chicken is done when the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and juices run clear.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the tandoori chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, keeping the chicken tender. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges, alongside mint chutney, naan bread, or a fresh salad.

tips: For a truly smoky flavor, you can add a piece of charcoal (heated until red hot) in a small metal bowl with a teaspoon of ghee and place it inside the covered container with the marinated chicken for 10-15 minutes before grilling. This is known as 'dhungar' technique.

Draining the yogurt is crucial; it removes excess water, allowing the marinade to cling better and prevents the chicken from becoming watery during grilling. If you dont have mustard oil, use a neutral oil, but mustard oil adds a distinct pungent flavor traditional to Tandoori dishes.

Tandoori chicken is best served immediately off the grill. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated gently in an oven or microwave, though the smoky flavor will be less pronounced.
